docs.title: The Systems Modeling Language v2
docs.text:
One of the interesting new capabilities is the exchange of models between tools using a human-readable textual form of the SysML language in the spirit of a modern programming language (even though it has a number of special constructs that resemble modelling concepts).

This textual form will play a major role in the exchange of models between tools thus allowing to build toolchains, as well as in the versioning of models, e.g., in GitHub, and also in the efficient definition of models by people who prepare textual notations.

It is therefore highly relevant to have consistent parsing mechanisms available. The SysML v2 Pilot-Implementation contains a parser for this textual notation.

We know from the definition of programming languages, that it is, however, helpful to provide a second source parser, such that parsing results can be compared and therefore compilers, linters, checkers of context conditions and other advanced tooling, receive the level of quality desired for industrial use.

docs.title: The SpesML v2 Functional Modeling Profile
docs.text:
In complex systems and software engineering, specifying functional behavior early in the design process is essential for ensuring correctness and consistency across development artifacts. However, existing modeling languages, including SysML v2, are often either too abstract or require premature commitment to implementation details, limiting the ability to capture partial specifications.

To overcome these limitations, we introduce a SysML v2 profile that embodies lessons learned from modeling with SysML v2. This profile restricts the broad SysML v2 language to a usable, semantically well-founded subset, while extending it with communication history-oriented specification constructs that leverage underspecification.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Let's start your SysML journey! In this chapter, we will show you how to start your first Project and introduce you to the basic concepts of SysML.

We provide documentation for both users who want to use the SysML v2 tool and developers who want to build or extend it.

  • For Users: Download and run the CLI tool.
  • For Developers: Build the tool from source and set up your development environment.

Found a problem with the documentation?

If you find an error or something is not understandable, please file an issue for it. This will help others reading the documentation in the future.

docs.title: Building the Tool from the Sources
docs.text:
As alternative to a download, it is possible to build an executable JAR of the tool from the source files located in GitHub. In order to build an executable Jar of the tool with Bash from the source files available in GitHub, execute the following commands.

First, clone the repository: 

git clone https://github.com/MontiCore/sysmlv2.git

Change the directory to the root directory of the cloned sources: 

cd sysmlv2

Then build the source files with gradle. To this effect, execute the following two command:

./gradlew :language:shadowJar
Please ensure that you have Java 21 JRE installed and gradle is set up to use it.

Congratulations! The executable JAR file language-7.*.*-SNAPSHOT-mc-tool.jar is now in the directory language/target/libs.

docs.title: Tools & Editors

docs.title: Setup SysML v2
docs.text: SysML v2 runs on any platform. In the following tutorials, we will use the CLI.

docs.title: Run the CLI
docs.text:
To run the CLI manually, you need to have Java 21 installed. Next, download the SysML v2 Tool jar.

You can then run the tool with:

java -jar MCSysMLv2.jar

exemplary usage:

java -jar MCSysMLv2.jar -h
java -jar MCSysMLv2.jar -i Car.sysml -pp

You can find detailed descriptions and available parameters in the usage section.

docs.title: Tool Download and Use
docs.text:
• Download SysML v2 Tool

The SysML v2 tool offers options for processing SysML v2 models. It provides through the CLI as follows:

java -jar MCSysMLv2.jar [-h] -i <fileName> [-path <p>] [-pp [<file>]] [-s [<file>]]

where the arguments are:

Option Explanation -ex,--extended Runs additional checks assuring the semantic soundness of models according to Spes -h,--help Prints this help dialog -i,--input <file> Reads the source file (mandatory) and parses the contents -path <arg> Sets the artifact path for imported symbols, space separated. -pp,--prettyprint <file> Prints the AST to stdout or the specified file (optional) -r,--report <dir> Prints reports of the artifact to the specified directory. -s,--symboltable <file> Serialized the Symbol table of the given artifact. -v,--version Prints version information

exemplary usage:

java -jar MCSysMLv2.jar -h
java -jar MCSysMLv2.jar -i Car.sysml -pp

docs.title: SpesML v2 Reference
docs.text:
Welcome to the SpesML v2 reference documentation. The SpesML v2 is constituted of a methodology and a SysML v2 language profile. From a technical perspective, the profile is an extension of the SysML expressions with:

  • Stream Library
  • OCL expressions
  • MontiCore type system based on Java types

docs.title: Stream Library & Writing Stream Specifications
docs.text: The Stream Library provides standard components and definitions for working with streams in SpesML. Here you can find stream expressions and the stream method library. The modeling with SpesML v2 works seamlessly with the MontiCore parser.

docs.title: Specifying Timing
docs.text:
Timing can be specified in multiple ways using user defined keywords:

  1. At the interface level over ports:

    #event port x;

  2. On the behavioral level:

    #sync satisfy requirement {...}

Warning

Note that 1. & 2. are mutually exclusive.

The default timing is event.

Stream specifications contain properties written over the input and output of components' ports.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Components use standard syntax and must declare its ports (packages beind optional): 

part def A {
  port input:   PortType1;
  port output: ~PortType1;

  ...
}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
Port types must exist and feature at least one attribute: 

port def PortType1 {
  attribute value: int;
}
Attribute types have to be standardized java types (int, double, float, short, long, boolean, byte, char, String), nat or user defined: 
attribute def UserDefinedType1 {
  attribute field1: int;
}


enum def UserDefinedEnum1 {
  enum E1;
  enum E2;
}

docs.title: Stream Specifications
docs.text:
Stream specifications can be expressed in SysML v2 as asserted constraints if there are no assumptions about the environment. 

assert constraint c1 {
  input.value == <1,2>
}
The stream of messages over a port can be recalled by field accesses over the port usage attribute. When accessed in specifications these field accesses have an implicit stream type. For example input.value in component A has the type EventStream<int>. In the case of port definitions with singular attributes we provide syntactic sugar by writing output instead of output.value as it is unambiguous that a stream access is. This is especially useful when chaining methods over streams.

More complex specifications can be written as assumption/guarantee pairs through requirements. Multiple assumptions and multiple guarantees are allowed. Each requirement corresponds to a property. 

satisfy requirement r1 {
  assume constraint c2 {
    input.value == <1>
  }
  require constraint c3 {
    output.value == input.value
  }
}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Stream specifications can also be parametrized with the parameter being set at initialization of the part. 

part A {
  ...

  final attribute maxValue: int;

  assert constraint c4 {
    input.value.first() >= maxValue;
  }
}

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
The stream method library and all stream expressions can be used inside specifications: 

output.value.length() == (input.value()^^<2>).length()

docs.title: OCLExpressions
docs.text:
It is usual to use first-order logic expressions in specifications. These can be embedded through OCLExpressions (which also include SetExpressions): 

forall t in nat:
  !input.value.nth(t).isEmpty() || input.values.nth(t) isIn {0}

docs.title: SpesML v2
docs.text: SpesML v2 is a modeling language based on the SPES framework currently in development. The SPES methodology defines a rigorous formal semantic applicable on the SysML v2 centered around specifying components through complete communication histories and stream-processing functions . The language shown below is a SysML v2 profile. There are currently two types of specifications supported: black-box through history-oriented specifications and glass-box through state machines.

docs.title: Exemplary Model: SumUp
docs.text:
The following model demonstrates a simple SumUp component specified in SpesML v2:

port def Naturals {
  in attribute val: nat;
}

part def SumUp {
  #untimed port x:  Naturals;
  #untimed port y: ~Naturals;

  satisfy requirement {
    assume constraint InfStream {
      x.hasInfiniteLen()
    }

    require constraint IncrementInplace {
      forall nat t:
        y.nth(t+1) == x.nth(t) + y.nth(t)
    }
  }
}

The SpesML v2 leverages underspecification as a core asset for high-level specifications, which can be thoroughly expressed through history-oriented stream-processing specifications. To this end we provide a stream library for stream processing functions which can be applied to streams.

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: Below is a list of error codes you might encounter while modeling using the CLI, along with explanations and suggestions on how to resolve them in your SysML models.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: A cardinality declaration is incomplete or empty.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Ensure your cardinalities conform to the format [n..m],or [m] where n is non-negative and m is non-negative with n <= m or * .

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: We deem cardinality ranges like [*], [n..*], or [n..m] problematic.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: We recommend using exact scalar cardinalities (e.g., [1]).

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Unresolved part usage, part definition, or port usage in a decomposed part def.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
...
part def A {
  connect somePart1.somePort to ...
}

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Check the names used in your connect statements to ensure the parts and ports exist and are spelled correctly. somePart1 has to be declared as a part usage with a type, it has to have a part def and somePort has to be declared in the definition of the part usage.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Unresolved Action definition or usage.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
action def A1: A {
  ...
}
action a: A2;

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Verify the spelling of the action and ensure it is defined in the current scope or imported. A and A2 here were not defined anywhere in scope. Please note that A must be an action def and A2 can be both an action def and a usage.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Specializations of port usages must be port usages or definitions.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Ensure the type assigned to your port is a valid port definition (see 0x10017).

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Unresolved Interface definition or usage.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Verify the spelling and existence of the referenced interface (see 0x10017).

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Unresolved Item definition or usage.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Verify the spelling and existence of the referenced item (see 0x10017).

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Unresolved Part or Port definition/usage.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Ensure that the parts and ports you are trying to specialize or type actually exist in the model (see 0x10017).

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Source or target state in a transition is not defined.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
state S;
transition first S then T;

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Verify that the first and then states S and T are declared in scope. In this case S is declared but T cannot be resolved.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Unresolved State definition.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Check the spelling of state definitions referenced in your models (see 0x10017).

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Part def used in refines specializations does not exist (SpesML specific CoCo).

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Check the spelling of the part definition you are trying to refine (see 0x10017).

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Illegal connection of (subcomponent) ports.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
port def SomePort {
  in attribute b: Boolean;
}
part def SomePart {
  port i:  SomePort;
  port o: ~SomePort;
}
part def A {
  port i1:  SomePort;
  port o1: ~SomePort;

  part sub:  SomePart;
  part sub1: SomePart;

  connect i1 to sub.i;  // 1
  connect sub.o to o1;  // 2
  connect i1 to sub.o1; // 3

  connect sub.o -> sub1.i; // 4
  connect sub.i -> sub1.o; // 5
}

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: We consider valid two types of simple connections: connecting subcomponent IO to other subcomponent IO of the opposite direction; connecting IO of subcomponents to the IO of the parent component with the same directionm, aka forwarding. Connections 1 and 2 are legal forwards. 3 is not. Connection 4 is valid, while 5 is not.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Subcomponent name is not unique.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Give each part usage within a block a unique name.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Failed to derive a type for an expression in constraints.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
port def SomePort {
  in attribute b: Boolean;
}
part def A {
  port i:  SomeBooleanIn;
  port o: ~SomeBooleanIn;

  constraint c {
    i.b > o.b
  }
}

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Check your expression for syntax errors or unresolved symbols. Here, the expressions on the left and right are not of type integer, which > requires.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Expression type should be boolean.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
port def SomePort {
  in attribute b: Integer;
}
part def A {
  port i:  SomeBooleanIn;

  exhibit state s {
    transition
    first S
    if i.b
    then S;
  }
}

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Ensure your constraint or transition guard evaluates to a true/false condition. Here the value of the guard is of type Integer.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: You are using a stream where a scalar value is expected.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
port def SomePort {
  in attribute b: Boolean;
}
part def A {
  port i:  SomeBooleanIn;
  port o: ~SomeBooleanIn;

  constraint c {
    i.b.first();
  }

  exhibit state s {
    transition
    first S
    if i.b.first()
    then S;
  }
}

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: in constraints access of a port evaluates stream based, while in transitions it evaluates to the explicit type. The expression in c is valid as i.b evaluates to EventStream<Boolean>, while in s to Boolean, making the guard invalid. See SpesML.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Cyclic specialization detected (e.g., part def A specializes B;, and part def B specializes A;).

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Specialization must be acyclic. Remove circular specialization relationships. This includes trivial specializations.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Symbol table serialization errors.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: This is an internal tool error usually caused by trying to serialize a construct that should not be serialized or of unknown timing. Ensure your model conforms strictly to supported SysML constructs.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Missing MontiCore specific standard library definitions. The tool failed to find or load the Stream.symtabdefinition from its resources.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Ensure all MontiCore Gradle dependencies are loaded.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: We do not recommend do actions in states.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Use entry, exit, or external transitions instead.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Name contains not recommended characters.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: For use in validation and verification tools, we recommend simple names. Rename the element using only letters, numbers, and underscores. Ensure it does not start with a number.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Port attribute does not have a type.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Ensure every attribute within a port definition has at least one type defined via : or defined by.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Discouraged use of flow connections.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Use standard connect or connection statements instead of flow.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Part should use at least one port.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: A well-modeled part should communicate with its environment. Add a port to your part definition.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Part has no explicit behavior.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Add a constraint, a state machine, or subparts to define the behavior of the part.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Part has conflicting behaviors.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
Ensure a part uses exactly one type of behavior specification (constraint, state machine, or composition), not a mixture of them.

Info

All other error codes describe internal errors and should be described through issues for assistance.
